text:
maria_support: FYI escalated from Acme Corp. Customer reports repeated SSE streams that either drop after ~90s or return partial outputs. They see EventSource errors client-side and a reconnect storm. Billing spike noticed because each reconnect counts as tokens. They provided repro steps below — can we triage?

maria_support: Repro from customer (copied):
1) open EventSource('/v1/streams?model=redwood-large') in browser (vanilla EventSource)
2) wait 60-120s, sometimes partial text arrives, then connection closes with network error.
3) client auto-reconnects immediately, then server sometimes resumes then cuts again.
4) token usage shows many small writes; customer thinks partial writes count as full responses.

maria_support: Attached logs (from their capture):
```
client: EventSource error: network error
server: [2027-05-21T14:12:01Z] stream write chunk: 128 bytes
server: [2027-05-21T14:13:31Z] connection closed by peer
nginx: upstream read timeout after 90.004s
ALB: Idle timeout expired
```

maria_support: They are behind an ALB with default idle timeout (60s?), and a Cloudflare worker in front. They also said some corporate proxies are present. Customer can't reproduce on localhost — only from their prod network.

maria_support: Requesting input from eng-runtime and infra: is this more likely ALB/proxy idle kills, or our SSE comment ping semantics? Also what to recommend to customer to reduce billing while we triage?

jon_eng_runtime: Thanks — looking. Quick hypothesis chain: (a) upstream LB/proxy idle timeout (b) proxy drops TLS and client sees EventSource error (c) server is still trying to write but kernel RST closes socket -> partial outputs. Also important: SSE spec allows sending comment frames (lines beginning with ":") as keepalive that don't create events. Some proxies treat long idle connections as dead regardless of data unless there is periodic TLS-level keepalive.

jon_eng_runtime: Question: are we sending any comment pings right now? And are we flushing after each write? If writes are buffered, proxies may still consider connection idle.

tara_infra: We saw similar with another customer where ALB default idle timeout was 60s and CloudFront at 120s. If there's an intermediate proxy with 90s read timeout, that'll close. Also note that some corporate proxies clobber HTTP/2 -> SSE fallback behavior.

li_devex: For customers using browser EventSource: recommend set reconnection backoff (EventSource auto-backoff sometimes is instant). Also suggest reducing token accounting by collapsing partial writes on server side (server should accumulate until coherent chunk or final event). We should provide a client-side example to avoid immediate reconnect loops.

sam_oncall: Ping deploy-bot for current service config.

deploy-bot: Runbook trigger: viewed service "streams-prod" -> pod replicas 6, proxy-read-timeout=90s, keepalive_timeout=60s, tcp_keepalive_os=default.

jon_eng_runtime: Ok that proxy-read-timeout=90s is suspicious. Two mitigation paths:
- short-term: instruct customer to accept comment pings every 25-30s (server will send a comment line ": ping\n\n") so proxies see activity. Also increase reconnection backoff client-side to jittered exponential.
- medium-term: change our streaming runtime to emit explicit comment pings at configurable interval when route has long tail latency. We need to be careful about token billing for comment pings (should be zero).

maria_support: Customer asks if comment pings will show up in their app or logs — are they visible to JS?

li_devex: Comment pings are SSE comments: they look like `:\n` or `: ping\n\n` and don't trigger message events. In browser EventSource they are invisible to `onmessage`. But they will be visible in raw network traces and in a proxy if it logs bytes.

jon_eng_runtime: Implementation notes for runtime: when we write comment pings, send exactly `:\n\n` (or `: keepalive\n\n`), then flush. On TLS, TCP keepalive operates at kernel level but is usually at multi-minutes default; that's not fast enough for 60-90s proxy timeouts. So application-layer comment pings are more reliable.

tara_infra: Also check upstream ALB settings: increase idle timeout to 300s for streaming routes. For k8s ingress with nginx we need `proxy_read_timeout` and `proxy_send_timeout` tuned. Example nginx snippet:```
proxy_read_timeout 360s;
proxy_send_timeout 360s;
proxy_buffering off;
chunked_transfer_encoding on;
```
Note: `proxy_buffering off` ensures we stream to client instead of buffering whole response.

maria_support: Customer also reported partial outputs counting toward billing. Is that handled by our billing pipeline?

jon_eng_runtime: We bill on tokens produced by the model invocation and bytes sent. If we stream intermediate tokens as separate write calls and the model restarted or connection dropped, the model tokens were already produced (billing-worthy). But we can mitigate client-side by batching small writes into larger frames where feasible, or our runtime can coalesce tokens for a short debounce (e.g., 200-500ms) before sending first bytes — tradeoff latency vs wasted tokens.

li_devex: For immediate customer fix: 1) ask them to configure their EventSource to exponential backoff (example below) 2) use a proxy-friendly keepalive: server side add comment ping every 25s 3) request ALB idle timeout bump if they control LB. Provide code sample:```js
// client-side naive backoff example
let es = new EventSource(url);
es.onopen = () => { backoff = 1000; }
es.onerror = () => { setTimeout(() => { es = new EventSource(url); }, backoff); backoff = Math.min(30000, backoff * 1.5 + Math.random() * 200); }
```

maria_support: Customer asked how to disable token billing for retries/spurious reconnections while we investigate — can we issue a temporary credit?

sam_oncall: Can approve small one-off credit pending case review. Suggest credit equal to 2x observed spike to be safe, and add note in case. I can do that once we confirm timeframe.

jon_eng_runtime: Action items for eng runtime:
- short patch: enable optional route-level keepalive comment pings with default 30s. Make sure we mark these pings as non-billable and not counted toward event tokens. Add a config flag `sse.keepalive_interval_ms`.
- medium: implement a small debounce/coalesce window for outgoing token writes configurable per-route.

tara_infra: Action items infra:
- check default proxy_read_timeout for ingress controllers and AWS ALB config for streaming endpoints. Consider a guided doc for customers and a console toggle to set streaming-friendly LB timeouts for Dedicated/Private fleets.

li_devex: I'll update docs with a troubleshooting section: "SSE clients show EventSource errors / partial outputs" and include steps: confirm path through proxies, enable comment pings, set proxy timeouts, client backoff pattern, and code snippets.

maria_support: Customer is OK with comment pings trial. They've asked for exact headers to set on server response.

jon_eng_runtime: Recommend headers:```
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Content-Type: text/event-stream
Cache-Control: no-cache, no-transform
Connection: keep-alive
Transfer-Encoding: chunked
X-Stream-Mode: chunked
```
Also ensure you flush after writes (server flush syscall) and do `setInterval(() => write(':\n\n'), 25000)` as a keepalive.

maria_support: Customer will try this out. For our side: can we add a monitoring alert if SSE route `last_byte_sent` < now - 2m while connection state is open?

jon_eng_runtime: Yes we'll add a metric `sse.connection_idle_seconds` and alert when >60s without application writes but connection is established. We'll also surface `sse.reconnect_rate` per-customer and tag by route.

maria_support: Thanks all. I'll relay patch plan and temporary credit approval to customer.

li_devex: Quick note: ensure comment pings are not incrementing event counters in telemetry; make telemetry drop lines starting with `:`.

jon_eng_runtime: Good catch — we'll filter them before counting. Also will add tests to simulate ALB close mid-stream and assert we don't double-count tokens in billing pipeline (or mark such cases for review).

maria_support: Closing loop: customer will test and report back within 24 hours. I'll re-open thread with their logs. :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: Deploy 2027-05-21T15:02:10Z: rolled runtime patch candidate to canary cluster (1/6 pods).

sam_oncall: I'll provision the credit after case ID review.

maria_support: Thanks team, leaving notes in the ticket.
